title: Private Deployments: VPC & On-Prem Deployment Guide, Day-2 Ops, Upgrade & Rollback, and Customer Requirements Library
summary: Consolidated reference for Redwood Private VPC and on-prem deployments: reference architectures, packaging and installation notes, day-2 operations, upgrade and rollback playbooks, and a customer requirements checklist.
overview: Purpose: This page is the canonical deployment reference for Redwood Private (VPC and on-prem) customers. Intended for Solutions Engineering, Customer Success, SRE and customer integrators responsible for onboarding, operating, and upgrading private deployments. The doc consolidates architecture options, packaging considerations, operational runbooks for day-2 tasks, and prescriptive upgrade/rollback procedures. It also contains a customer requirements library used during scoping.
scope: Covered: VPC-hosted private control plane with customer networking, air-gapped on-prem packaging and install, recommended reference architectures for small/medium/large footprints, day-2 ops (monitoring, alerts, backups, scaling), detailed upgrade & rollback procedures, and a standard customer requirements checklist. Not covered: vendor-specific network configuration beyond examples, customer-specific compliance attestations, or Dedicated managed service variants.
reference_architectures: Supported patterns: 1) VPC: Customer VPC with private subnets, NAT/egress, optional private endpoint to Redwood control plane, bastion host, customer-managed KMS, optional transit gateway. Typical services: internal load balancers, managed K8s (EKS/GKE), stateful PV storage (EBS/PD), object store (S3-compatible), monitoring endpoints. Scale tiers: small (1 replica inference pool, 8x A10x-style GPUs), medium (3 replica pools, mixed T4/A10x), large (multi-AZ >8 GPU servers, autoscaler tuning). 2) On-Prem: Customer datacenter or co-located racks, orchestration (K8s/OpenShift), offline package bundle (OCI tarball, Helm charts, signed manifests), HSM/KMS integration, physical NIC config for RDMA. Packaging: signed artifact bundle with checksums, install script, and validation harness; offline license token and support bundle upload mechanism included.
packaging_and_installation: Packaging options: Cloud/VPC: Helm charts + kustomize overlays + post-install operator; images pulled from Redwood private registry or customer mirror via authenticated pull secrets. On-Prem (air-gapped): tarball of OCI images, Helm chartmuseum tarballs, install.sh, kubeconfig bootstrap helper, and offline package checklist. Pre-install checklist example: confirm Kubernetes version (recommended 1.24-1.27), GPU drivers (NVIDIA 520+), container runtime (containerd 1.6+), CSI storage class present, validated CNI, KMS/HSM endpoints and certs available, firewall rules for outbound egress or offline license activation.
networking_and_security_requirements: Minimum network: internal DNS for service discovery. Critical ports: 443 for HTTPS, 8080 for internal metrics, 9090 for Prometheus scrape endpoints, plus runtime gRPC ports (per-customer manifest). Security controls: TLS everywhere and mTLS for service-to-service traffic, support for customer-managed certs. KMS & secrets: AWS KMS, HashiCorp Vault, and customer HSM via PKCS#11 supported. Audit & logging: Fluentd/Vector collectors recommended; logs forwarded to customer SIEM.
day_2_operations: Ownership: primary teams include customer-platform (customer), Redwood support (escalation), eng-sre (playbook maintenance). Monitoring & alerting: core metrics include per-model latency P50/P95, token throughput, GPU utilization, pod restart count, KV cache hit rate. SLO examples: 99th percentile tail latency < 300ms for small models under steady-state for dedicated pools (customer SLA may differ). Alerts: GPU OOM rate > 0.5% sustained (P3m), pod crashloop > 5 times in 10 minutes, disk pressure > 80%. Routine tasks: Daily: check health dashboard, review critical alerts, verify backup success. Weekly: rotate short-lived certs, review cost and scaling metrics, verify KV cache efficiency reports. Monthly: simulated failover and recovery drill in staging, refresh offline packages if required.
backup_and_restore: Configuration backups: etcd snapshots (K8s), Postgres metadata backups, object store retention policies. Model artifacts: stored in object store; verify immutability and replication settings. Restore procedure (high level): validate restore target cluster, restore etcd snapshot, reapply CRDs and workloads, validate model index and KV cache warmup.
scaling_and_capacity_guidance: Horizontal scaling: inference pool autoscaler based on concurrent requests and queued request depth. Suggested target GPU utilization: 65-75% for cost-efficiency. Vertical scaling: increase GPU types for larger model families; validate threads/streams per-GPU kernel configuration and NUMA affinity settings.
upgrade_and_rollback_procedures: Upgrade strategy: canary-first progressive rollout with automated health checks. Pre-upgrade checklist: snapshot etcd, verify backups, collect pre-upgrade metrics and golden prompts/eval suite, ensure rollback image/package available. Upgrade steps example: 1) Prepare: create release branch, publish images to customer registry, sign manifests. 2) Stage canary: deploy new control-plane components to a single canary namespace/node pool. 3) Validate canary: synthetic smoke tests, golden prompts, validate latency and correctness thresholds. 4) Progressive rollout: 10% -> 30% -> 60% -> 100% with 15-30 minute stabilization windows. 5) Post-validation: run full suite, confirm model serving and KV cache behavior, notify stakeholders. Rollback playbook: Trigger conditions include canary failure, error budget burn > 5% in 15m, or critical stability regressions. Immediate steps: pause rollout in automation (Argo Rollouts/Flux/Helm operator), revert to last-known-good manifests and images, restore etcd snapshot if incompatible schema migrations occurred, execute post-rollback smoke tests and verify metrics return to baseline. Rollback validation: validate latencies, error rates, and golden prompt end-to-end tests before closing incident.
customer_requirements_library: Standard scoping items captured by SE intake form: Minimal required: point of contact (name, email, oncall), cluster type & version (EKS/GKE/self-managed OpenShift), expected QPS and model mix (text-gen/embeddings/reranking), peak concurrent requests and average token length, network topology (VPC CIDR, peering, transit gateway), firewall rules, authentication and KMS choice (AWS KMS/customer HSM/Vault), compliance constraints (data residency, encryption-at-rest), backup retention and RPO/RTO expectations. Optional/extended: RDMA/NIC offload capability, GPU model preference, preferred observability stack (Prometheus/Datadog/Splunk), allowed egress endpoints (air-gapped whitelist steps), maintenance windows and change control process.
checklists_and_playbooks: Pre-install one-line: confirm pre-install checklist items in packaging_and_installation. Day-2 ops quick checklist: validate health dashboard, confirm backups successful, review active alerts and paging status, verify autoscaler is healthy. Upgrade quick playbook: snapshot state, deploy canary, run golden prompt suite, monitor for regressions, escalate and rollback if thresholds exceeded.

troubleshooting_and_known_issues: Common symptom: high tail latency after deployment. Quick checks: KV cache warmup, GPU oversubscription, model quantization mismatch. Remediations: warm caches, scale up GPU pool, revert quantization profile. Common symptom: image pull failures (air-gapped). Quick checks: verify image tarball checksums, registry mirror credentials, and storage permissions.
appendix: Example Helm upgrade command: helm upgrade --install redwood --namespace redwood --values values-prod.yaml redwood/redwood-chart --timeout 15m. Example etcd snapshot: ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl snapshot save /tmp/etcd-snap.db --endpoints=${ETCD_ENDPOINT} --cacert=/etc/kubernetes/pki/ca.crt --cert=/etc/etcd/peer.crt --key=/etc/etcd/peer.key. Golden prompts smoke test (curl): curl -sS -X POST https://localhost:443/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -d '{"prompt":"The capital of France is"}'.
